records.label: Theorem
records.quote: In the same circle, the measures of all inscribed angles subtended by the same arc are equal in measure.
records.claim: In the same circle, the measures of all inscribed angles subtended by the same arc are equal in measure.

records.stem: Given: ∠C, ∠D and ∠E are common inscribed angles at arc AB. R.T.P.: m(∠C) = m(∠D) = m(∠E)

records.label: Example
records.quote: In the opposite figure : AB ∩ CD = {E} , EA = ED
records.stem: In the opposite figure: $\overline{AB}\cap\overline{CD}=\{E\}$, $EA=ED$. Prove that: $EB=EC$.
solution: ∵ ∠ABC, ∠ADC are both inscribed and include arc AC ∴ $m(\angle B)=m(\angle D)$ (2)
∵ ∠DCB, ∠DAB are both inscribed and include arc BD ∴ $m(\angle C)=m(\angle A)$ (3)
From (1), (2) and (3) we deduce that: $m(\angle B)=m(\angle C)$

records.claim: In the same circle or in congruent circles, the measures of the inscribed angles subtended by arcs of equal measures are equal.

records.label: Example
records.quote: AD and BE are two equal chords in length in the circle
records.stem: In the opposite figure: $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{BE}$ are two equal chords in length in the circle, $\overrightarrow{AD}\cap\overrightarrow{BE}=\{C\}$. Prove that: $CD=CE$.
solution: by adding $m(\widehat{DE})$ to each of the two sides, we get: $m(\widehat{ADE})=m(\widehat{BED})$
By subtracting the two sides of (2) from (1) we get: $CD=CE$
records.notes: Solution text is blurry; transcribed as read. Step 'AD = BE' in line 1 and 'AD = BF' in (2) read from blurry print; verify.

records.quote: If two angles subtended to the same base and on the same side
records.claim: The converse of theorem 2: if two angles are subtended to the same base and on the same side of it, and have the same measure, then their vertices lie on an arc of a circle and the base is a chord in it.

records.text: In the opposite figure, notice that: ∠C, ∠D are both drawn on the base AB, and on one side of it, m(∠C) = m(∠D). Then: The points A, B, C and D lie on one circle where AB is a chord in it.

objectives.label: Infer equality of inscribed angles on the same arc
objectives.description: Find and use the fact that inscribed angles subtended by the same arc in a circle are equal in measure.

objectives.label: Apply the theorem to find angle measures and prove relations
objectives.description: Use equal inscribed angles to find unknown angles and prove segment or angle relations in circle figures.

objectives.label: Relate inscribed angles to equal arcs
objectives.description: Decide that inscribed angles subtended by arcs of equal measure are equal in the same or congruent circles, and the converse.

objectives.label: Decide whether four points lie on one circle
objectives.description: Use equal angles on the same base and same side to show that points are concyclic.
